verdicts.reason: A fills the banner well with a strong headline and a clean centred axis. But the subhead is oversized at about 60% of the headline's size, so it competes with the headline and crowds it, and the stack has tight vertical gaps. B is just a shrunk copy of the original: the headline floats in big empty lime margins and the subhead and CTA text are small for this size.

A tries a left-to-right banner split, but its alignment is sloppy. The two-line headline is centred while the wider subhead below it is left-aligned at a different edge. The subhead is too large and sits close to the bottom, and the CTA floats alone on the right with no shared baseline. B is a clean, centred copy that is merely shrunk, with small secondary text and too much dead space.

A jams the headline against the left canvas edge at about 12px. The subhead is indented to a different edge (x≈70) and the CTA to a third (x≈38), so nothing shares a left edge. It is oversized and leaves the right side empty, which makes the layout lopsided. B is a tidy, centred, faithful resize, though shrunk and under-scaled, with small subhead and button text.
